holes.name: The Washington Memorial
holes.description: The opening hole at Baylake Pines sets the tone for your round. A strategic 75-foot approach that demands precision over power. The towering loblolly pine guards the basket, creating a natural cathedral that commands respect from every player who steps to the tee.
holes.story: Standing on this tee box, you're not just playing disc golf—you're walking in the footsteps of history. The magnificent loblolly pine before you was planted in 1799 to honor America's first president, George Washington, the year of his passing. For 227 years, this sentinel has stood watch over Baylake Pines, surviving hurricanes, wars, and the passage of time. Local legend holds that the tree was planted by a Revolutionary War veteran who served under Washington himself, a living monument to the father of our country. Today, it serves as the crown jewel of our first hole, reminding every player that some things—like honor, tradition, and a well-thrown disc—are timeless.
holes.nameStory: Crown jewel of loblolly pine trees supposedly planted in 1799 as a memorial to George Washington. This majestic tree stands as a silent witness to over two centuries of neighborhood history.
